title: A root literal scalar set to text with no final line break changes only its header to strip
notes: The empty pointer addresses the whole document. The old value is `old` and one final line break under clip chomping. The new value `n` has no final line break, so the header must become `|-` for it to read back exactly (see Setters are exact); the marker, the content indentation and the final line break of the input stay. A root literal behaves like `edit/block-literal-strip-when-no-trailing-newline`, which pins the same step for a mapping value.

provenance.reference: Differential testing of the oneyaml-python native and pure backends; the native backend dropped the literal style and wrote a plain scalar, `--- n`; the pure backend wrote the expected bytes.
